body:
Nixodine devices are used and stored like other rechargeable disposables, and the habits that keep them working well are the same ones that apply to any small lithium-battery device. This guide covers what to do before first use, how to use a device gently, how to store it, how to care for the battery, how to keep it away from children and pets, how to troubleshoot common problems and how to dispose of it. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. We make no health claims about Nixodine or any product, and regulatory treatment of newer ingredients can change, so always check the label and your local rules.

## Before first use
Remove packaging and any protective film from the mouthpiece and the charging port. Check that the device is not damaged, swollen or leaking. Charge it if the battery is low, using a standard USB-C cable and a basic 5V adapter. See [charging a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/). Read the label: check the strength as the manufacturer writes it, the warnings and any instructions. Make sure you are 21 or older, and that you are somewhere that use is allowed.

## Using it
Draw gently. Take breaks between puffs, as chain use can heat the coil and shorten flavor life. A slow, steady draw gives the best flavor, and a very hard draw can pull liquid through too fast. If your device has adjustable airflow or power modes, start with the lower setting. See [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/) and [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/). Do not use a device that is hot, cracked or leaking.

### Habits that protect flavor
- **Do not chain vape.** Let the wick re-saturate between puffs.
- **Keep it upright** when not in use.
- **Avoid leaving it in heat or direct sun.**
- **Wipe the mouthpiece** if it gets wet.
- **Take breaks** during long sessions.

## Storing
Keep devices cool, dry and upright. See [how to store disposables](/blog/how-to-store-disposable-vapes/). Do not leave them in a hot car, on a windowsill or near a heater. Store spares in their packaging, in a cupboard away from sunlight. If you buy a 5-pack, keep the spares sealed until you need them, and use the oldest first. Check devices occasionally for damage or swelling.

## Battery care
Avoid heat and charge on a hard surface. See [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/) and [how to make your vape battery last longer](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/). Charge when the battery is low, not when it is completely flat, and unplug when full. Do not leave a device charging overnight or unattended. Do not use a damaged cable or an unbranded charger. If a device gets hot, swells or smells odd, stop using it and take it for recycling.

## Children and pets
Keep devices out of reach; see [storage tips](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/). Store them in a closed cupboard or a lockable box, not on tables or in bags that children can reach. Finished devices are also a hazard, so keep them out of reach until you dispose of them. If a child or pet is exposed to liquid or swallows a part, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 or a veterinarian immediately.

## Traveling
Devices and batteries must travel in carry-on baggage on flights, and you may not use them on board. See [traveling with vapes](/blog/traveling-with-vapes-airline-rules/). Pack a device switched off, away from keys and coins, and check the rules at your destination.

## Disposal
When it is empty, recycle responsibly; see [disposal](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Take finished devices to a hazardous waste or electronics recycling site. Do not put them in household trash, and do not try to open them. Tape over any exposed terminals if the device is damaged, and keep it in a sealed bag until you drop it off.

## Troubleshooting
If it stops working, see [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/). Common causes are a flat battery, a blocked airflow, a flooded coil or the end of the liquid. If it will not charge, see [what to do when a vape will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/). If it leaks, see [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/). If it gurgles, see [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/).

## When to contact us
If a device from us is faulty from new, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID, a description and photos or a short video. Our [refund policy](/refunds/) explains what applies. If it arrives damaged, photograph the items and the invoice straight away and email us. See [damaged or missing items](/blog/damaged-or-missing-items-what-to-do/).

## Claims
We make no health claims about Nixodine or any product, and regulatory treatment of newer ingredients can change, so always check the label and your local rules. Read the label for the active ingredient and warnings. If you are unsure about anything, ask us before you use a product.

## A simple routine
Keep the device in a pocket or a case, upright where you can. Charge it once it is low, on a hard surface, while you are nearby. Store spares in a cool cupboard. Check dates and condition monthly. Take finished devices to a recycling site. A routine like this keeps devices working and keeps your household secure.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### How long does a device last?
It depends on capacity and your use. Puff counts are estimates. Heavy use shortens it.

### Can I use it while it charges?
Only if the manual says pass-through is supported. Otherwise wait until charging is done.

### Why does it taste weaker after a while?
Palate adaptation, a worn coil or the end of the liquid. Rotate flavors and take breaks.

### Can I leave it in my car?
Not for long. Heat damages batteries and flavor. Keep it with you.

### What do I do with spares?
Store them sealed, in a cool cupboard, away from children and pets.

## Shop
Browse [Nixodine products](/shop/nixodine/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over.

## A worked example of a month with three devices
You buy three devices: one for daily use, one in your bag and one spare in a cupboard. The daily device is charged every second evening on a hard surface, while you are nearby. The bag device stays in a case, away from keys. The spare stays sealed in a cool cupboard. After two weeks the daily device is finished, so you take it to a recycling site, and open the spare. You note the date in your phone so you know when to replace the bag device. Nothing is left lying around, and nothing is wasted.

## Common mistakes
- **Leaving devices in a hot car.**
- **Charging overnight.**
- **Chain vaping.**
- **Leaving a finished device in a drawer.**
- **Opening a device to see what is inside.**
- **Storing devices where children or pets can reach them.**

Avoiding these keeps devices working and your household secure.

## Checking a device before use
Look at the casing for dents or swelling. Check that the mouthpiece is clean and the charging port is free of lint. Make sure the airflow is not blocked. If anything looks wrong, do not use it, and contact us if the device is new. A 20-second check each time you open a new device can prevent a lot of trouble.

## Keeping records
Keep your order confirmation, the invoice and any photos of the device. They help if you ever need to contact us about a problem. If you buy several devices, label each with the date you opened it, so that you can track how long each lasts. That information helps you choose the right capacity next time.

## Frequently asked questions about use and storage
### Can I share a device with someone?
Please do not. Nicotine-related products are for adults, and sharing is not advisable. Each person should use their own.

### Should I clean a disposable?
Wipe the outside with a dry cloth. Do not open it or put it in water.

### What if a device is left in the sun?
Move it to a cool place, let it cool fully and check it for swelling. If it looks damaged, stop using it and recycle it.

### How do I know the battery is failing?
It drains much faster than before, charges slowly or gets warm when idle. Stop using it if you see swelling or odd smells.

## A short guide to a steady routine
Build a routine that does not depend on remembering: one place for charging, one place for storage, one bin or bag for finished devices and a monthly check of what you have. Teach everyone in the household where products go, and agree that none is left lying around. A routine like this keeps devices working and keeps risks low, and it takes only a few seconds each day.

## Final reminders
Keep devices away from children and pets, charge them with care, store them cool and dry, never open them and recycle them when finished. If anything seems wrong, stop using the device and contact us. All products are for adults aged 21 and over.

### One last tip
Write the date you open a device on a small piece of tape on its box, or in a note on your phone. Knowing how long each device lasts helps you choose the right capacity next time, and it helps you notice if something is wearing out faster than it should.

faq.q: What should I do before first use?
faq.a: Remove packaging, check the device for damage, charge it if needed, read the label for strength and warnings and make sure you are 21 or older.
Draw gently, take breaks between puffs and avoid chain use. Do not use a hot, cracked or leaking device.
Cool, dry and upright, away from heat, sunlight, children and pets.

faq.q: How do I care for the battery?
faq.a: Avoid heat, charge on a hard surface, unplug when full and never leave it charging unattended.

faq.q: How do I dispose of a finished device?
faq.a: Take it to a hazardous waste or electronics recycling site. Do not put it in household trash or try to open it.

faq.q: What if my device is faulty?
faq.a: Contact us with your order ID and a description. See the refund policy.
